extra.message: Student.create() uses Python string interpolation to build SQL: VALUES ('%(name)s') % {'name': name}. The name parameter comes from user input (request.post()['name'] in views.py:57) and is inserted directly into the SQL string, allowing SQL injection attacks that can bypass constraints, extract data, or modify other rows/tables.

Jinja2 autoescape is set to False in app.py:35. Combined with templates like course.jinja2 ({{ course.title }} and {{ course.description }} on lines 14-15 without |e filter), stored XSS is possible. User-controlled data submitted via POST (e.g., course title/description in views.courses:89-90) is rendered unescaped in templates, enabling stored XSS attacks in the browser.

Csrf middleware is commented out in app.py:27 (csrf_middleware is commented out with # csrf_middleware). The csrf_middleware function exists in sqli/middlewares.py:26-38 but is never applied to the app. Without CSRF protection, authenticated users can be tricked into submitting POST requests on behalf of the attacker (e.g., creating students/courses, submitting reviews, evaluating students on their behalf), especially since session cookies lack the HttpOnly flag (see sqli/middlewares.py:20).

RedisStorage is created with httponly=False in middlewares.py:20. This allows JavaScript (including XSS payloads) to read the session cookie via document.cookie, making XSS attacks more exploitable - session hijacking becomes trivial without HttpOnly protection.

User.check_password() uses MD5 (no salt, no iterations) to hash passwords: md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest() on lines 40-41. MD5 is cryptographically broken and can be brute forced in seconds. An attacker with database access can trivially reverse all user passwords.

views.students() on line 51 has no @authorize() decorator and no auth check. Any unauthenticated user can POST to /students/ (views.students:54-57) to create arbitrary students, and can access /students/{id} (views.student:66-68). Similarly, views.courses() at line 83 lacks authentication. This allows any client to access all student/course data, modify it, and perform all available actions without authentication.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Course review text is rendered in course template (course.jinja2:22: {{ review.review_text }}) without |e escaping filter. With autoescape=False set in sqli/app.py:35, user-supplied review text submitted via views.review (sqli/views.py:119-129) is rendered as raw HTML/JS in subsequent page views, creating stored XSS.

Course title rendered in review template (review.jinja2:32: {{ course.title }}) without |e filter. With autoescape=False (sqli/app.py:35), and course titles being insertable by attackers (views.courses:89-90), this enables stored XSS when any user visits the review page for that course.

User.check_password() uses MD5 to hash passwords: md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest() on line 40-41. MD5 is broken against collision resistance and brute-force attacks. With no salt, identical passwords produce same hash allowing rainbow table attacks across users.

views.course() at line 96 has no @authorize() or auth check. Any anonymous user can access all course reviews and other student information (views.course:104-105: reviews and students are loaded and returned to any requester). This exposes private review data and student information to unauthenticated users.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: views.review() at line 111 has no @authorize() or auth check. Any unauthenticated user can access course review pages and create reviews (views.review:119-129) by submitting POST requests. This enables unauthenticated review creation (spam, attacks, manipulation).

extra.message: views.evaluate() at line 134 has no @authorize() or authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can POST to /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id} and assign grades to any student (sqli/views.py:151: await Mark.create(conn, student_id, course_id, data['points'])). This enables arbitrary grade manipulation by unauthenticated users.
